jupas.shortDescription: an class="before_label">Short Description The Bachelor of Laws (LLB) is a four-year programme that offers intellectual and personal development through the medium of law. Students will explore a range of engaging and important subjects, while developing their critical analysis and creative problem-solving skills and enhancing their ability to construct detailed, well-reasoned, compelling arguments. These are life-long skills that will support graduates in whatever careers they choose, be they in law or other fields. The first two years are almost entirely focused on compulsory subjects, grouped into the themes of Foundations of Law, Public Law (which governs relations between the state and citizens) and Obligations (which governs relations between citizens). In their final two years, students will combine a few remaining compulsory subjects with courses they select from a range of electives, allowing students to develop further expertise in legal areas of their choice. Students may also choose to specialize in the Global Law or Chinese Law streams, indicated a degree of specialization in that particular area that will be reflected on their transcripts. LLB students have a few opportunities to obtain double degrees. Please visit the Faculty website for further details.

cuhkAdmission.introduction: Explore an Exciting Journey in Our Bachelor of Laws Programme Our Bachelor of Laws (LLB) programme provides world-class academic and professional education in law. Students learn the rules and values underpinning the law and its role in structuring society through extensive reading, thinking, writing, discussing and debating. Our approach to legal education emphasises persuasion, problem solving, analysing complex issues, dispute management and reflecting on competing viewpoints. The legal knowledge and critical thinking skills you gain will be with you for the rest of your life and will allow you to be successful at the highest level in the legal field or any other professional path you choose, whether in Hong Kong or elsewhere around the world.
cuhkAdmission.careerProspects: After completing our LLB program, you will satisfy one of the admission requirements for the Postgraduate Certificate in Laws (PCLL) in Hong Kong. In recent years, on average, 80% of CUHK LLB graduates who sought a place in the PCLL program were successful. You are eligible for admission as a Solicitor or Barrister of the High Court of Hong Kong after completing the PCLL, and a training contract (2 years) or pupillage (1 year). Our LLB graduates are well equipped to be legal practitioners or leaders in other fields, such as commerce, industry, government, community service, academia and media. Employers include major international law firms (e.g., A&O Shearman, Baker McKenzie, Clifford Chance, Deacons, DLA Piper, Fangda Partners, Freshfields Bruckhaus Deringer, Herbert Smith Freehills, Hogan Lovells, Johnson Stokes & Master, King & Wood Mallesons, Linklaters, Morrison Foerster, Norton Rose Fulbright, Slaughter & May, and Zhong Lun Law Firm LLP), the Hong Kong
cuhkAdmission.craftYourPath: aging and transformative. We provide a liberal education in the theory and practice of law at the level of rigour appropriate to an undergraduate programme of study. Our LLB programme is designed for critical and creative thinkers who are ready to become leaders in law or related fields, who want to be successful in the increasingly globalised legal arena, and who are dedicated to serving society. Double-Degree Study Options Bachelor of Laws (LLB) Double Degree Programmes at CUHK Students can register for one of the following double-degree options towards the end of their first year of studies: (i)  LLB with a Bachelor of Arts in Translation (ii) LLB with a Bachelor of Social Science in Sociology Master of Laws (LLM) Programme at the Dickson Poon School of Law of King’s College London Master of Laws (LLM) Programme at the University of Southern California Gould School of Law CUHK LAW offers two joint study options in partnership with King’s College London (KCL) and the University of Southern California (USC). Under these options, students may enrol in the Master of Laws (LLM) Programme at KCL or USC in their fourth year. This provides students with an opportunity to obtain both an undergraduate degree (LLB from CUHK) and a postgraduate degree (LLM from KCL or USC) in four years.
